On a system with i386 enabled, apt update prints: "N: Skipping acquire of configured file 'main/binary-i386/Packages' as repository '... stable InRelease' doesn't support architecture 'i386'". It's harmless, but noisy. The repo is amd64 only.

Do:

Keep the two identical (the publisher's local test compares them; update the test if it needs it). Keep the fingerprint-first steps unchanged.
- Add a line in the README telling existing users to edit /etc/apt/sources.list.d/cosmic-ext-nightlight.list the same way if they want the notice gone.
- Add a CHANGELOG line under the unreleased/next entry. Do not bump the version again unless the changelog layout needs it; do not release.

The clauses this work was bound by:

1. C2: Before finishing, every engineer runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `cargo clippy --all-targets` with no new warnings, besides the tests.

From `6db778d492` to `04483c96d7`. The whole diff is in [changes.diff](changes.diff). The conversation, shortened, is in [transcript.jsonl](transcript.jsonl); [the README](../README.md) explains the files.

- [k3] `just deb` runs `cargo deb --locked` (needs `cargo install cargo-deb`) and writes target/debian/*.deb. Config is in Cargo.toml [package.metadata.deb]. Depends is `$auto, cosmic-panel, cosmic-comp`; the cosmic-* package names are unchecked against a COSMIC apt repo. The libc6 floor comes from the build host, so build on the oldest target distro.
- [k4] Releases: .github/workflows/release.yml has build (no secrets), sign (environment `release`) and publish (contents: write) jobs. just and cargo-deb are pinned by hand to exact versions. The README fingerprint placeholder must be replaced with the real signing-key fingerprint before the first v* tag; the build job fails while it is there.
- [k5] release.yml fails if README.md contains the fingerprint placeholder text (grep for 'FINGERPRINT-TO-BE-FILLED-IN'). Don't write that exact token anywhere else in the README, or a filled-in README would still fail.
- [k10] libcosmic's `applet` feature links GPL-3.0-only crates from pop-os/cosmic-panel (cosmic-panel-config, xdg-shell-wrapper-config). Their Cargo.toml has no license field, so license tools show them blank. Check with `cargo tree -i cosmic-panel-config`.
- [k11] Release state on GitHub can be read without credentials: curl https://api.github.com/repos/deepthinker2001/cosmic-ext-nightlight/actions/runs, then each run's jobs_url and check-run annotations give each job's failure reason. As of 2026-11-13 no release has published the apt repository (gh-pages is empty).
- [k12] scripts/publish-apt.sh can be tested locally without a real key: make a throwaway ed25519 key in a temporary GNUPGHOME and a dummy .deb with dpkg-deb --build, then run the script on an empty site folder.
- [k13] THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES is generated by `just notices` (scripts/gen-third-party-notices.py) from Cargo.lock; regenerate it when Cargo.lock changes. The script reads license files only from inside the crate or its git checkout, since git checkouts keep symlinks.
- [k14] Iced-Icons.ttf (compiled in by iced_graphics) holds six Font Awesome glyphs (SIL OFL 1.1, Dave Gandy, picked through Fontello) and the iced logo (MIT). Its OFL notice is data/licenses/OFL-FontAwesome.txt; re-check it if iced_graphics changes the font. cargo-deb is installed here: `cargo deb --locked` then `dpkg-deb -c target/debian/*.deb` checks the package contents (release build about 75…
- [k15] Release is a push to main whose Cargo.toml version has no v<version> tag: the build job decides (step-level ifs), attach creates the tag and release at the built commit and checks the tag's commit, apt signs. The release environment should allow only branch main (no Tag rule); v* tag creation stays restricted, with a bypass for the Actions app (unverified on GitHub). To release: bump versi…
- [k18] The apt landing page (index.html) is a quoted HTML heredoc in scripts/publish-apt.sh; keep its pinned fingerprint and install commands in step with README.md. An existing site gets changes only through a release or a manual workflow run from main with an existing tag, since the publisher comes from main.
- [k19] Releases and CI run on ubuntu-24.04, never ubuntu-latest, because cargo-deb takes the libc6 floor from the build host's glibc. scripts/check-deb-libc.py fails a release whose libc6 floor is above 2.39. When raising the oldest supported Ubuntu, change both runners and the 2.39 limit in the script together.

To update to a new version: `sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade`, or just
install your system updates as usual.

Already added the repository? To remove apt's harmless notice about missing
`i386` packages, edit `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/cosmic-ext-nightlight.list`
with administrator privileges and add `arch=amd64` before `signed-by` inside
the brackets, as above. The repository provides amd64 packages only.

## Unreleased

- Apt setup instructions now specify `arch=amd64` to avoid the harmless
  missing-i386 notice on multiarch systems; the README explains how existing
  users can update their sources line.
